direct_claims: This chart compares undernourishment with average daily calorie supply across countries and regions.
It belongs to the food security and nutrition domain.
The title states the comparison is between the share of people who are undernourished and daily supply of calories.
The expert domain story defines undernourishment here as the share of the total population with caloric intakes below minimum energy requirements.
The image credits Our World in Data and cites the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations as the data source.
In this domain, undernourishment is not simply hunger reported in surveys; it is an estimate based on whether people’s caloric intake falls below minimum energy requirements.
Average daily supply of calories refers to kilocalories available per person per day, as stated on the x-axis in the image.
The chart note says values between 0% and 2.5% are shown as 2.5%, so very low-undernourishment places are visually grouped at that floor rather than distinguished precisely.
In the visible table excerpt, low-income economies have 28.4% undernourishment, while high-income economies are listed at 2.5%.
In the visible table excerpt, Eastern Africa is 25.9%, Middle Africa is 30.2%, and Northern Africa is 10.7%, showing substantial within-Africa variation.
In the visible table excerpt, Africa overall is 20.2%, Asia is 6.7%, the Americas are 3.2%, and Oceania is 7.6%.
This data matters because undernourishment tracks whether populations are meeting minimum dietary energy needs.

Populations in low-income and food-deficit settings are especially affected, as shown by high values in categories such as low-income economies at 28.4%, low income food deficit countries at 24.8%, and least developed countries at 21.7% in the visible table excerpt.
Because the metadata table is truncated and the calorie values are blank in the excerpt, some chart interpretations depend on reading the image rather than calculating from the table.
